messages:
Maya (support): FYI customer (ACME) is seeing intermittent 502/504s hitting Hosted API for bulk embeddings ingestion. Started ~10:02 UTC, ~30% requests fail. Repro steps attached by customer.
Liam (eng-sre): Can you paste a sample request id + any x-envoy headers from traces? Might be upstream ejection or TLS flapping.
Maya (support): sample trace: x-request-id=REQ-7c2b4a, x-envoy-upstream-service-time=12000, x-redwood-region=us-west-2. Customer says burst is long-lived streaming upload (chunks every 200ms) from a single client IP.
Sofia (eng-platform): Noted. Recent config change last night touched Envoy outlier detection and ejection thresholds for rlb (region load balancer). Rolling back to previous thresholds for the region would be quick if this looks like ejections.
Raj (eng-runtime): Long-lived streams + high request concurrency can exhaust upstream connection windows. If Envoy outlier ejects a host while autoscaler is spinning up new Dedicated pods, we can hit a transient capacity gap -> 502s/504s. Any autoscaler logs?
Maya (support): Customer gave a curl repro: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <tok>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @large_payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings` They split into 6 streamed chunks.
infra-bot: ALERT: rlb-us-west-2: host ejection rate spike detected (2026-02-18T10:01:54Z) — 8 hosts ejected in 60s :eyes:
Liam (eng-sre): That bot alert aligns. Can we check envoy clusters for rlb-us-west-2? `curl -s http://envoy-admin/cluster?format=json | jq '.clusters[] | select(.name=="rlb-us-west-2")'` — look for `circuit_breakers` and `outlier_detection` events in logs.
Sofia (eng-platform): I see the staged change: outlier_detection.success_rate.minimum_hosts was lowered to 3 which can be too aggressive when a single AZ sees streaming bursts. Rolling that parameter back now.
Raj (eng-runtime): Also check h2 keepalive: we had a tweak to reduce keepalive_timeout for streaming endpoints — could be triggering premature connection closes with some client patterns. Suggest revert and monitor.
Nina (prod): Pinned a canary rollback for rlb-us-west-2 at 10:06 UTC. I also enabled a temporary routing policy to prefer healthy hosts in us-east-1 for embeddings ingestion while we stabilize.
Maya (support): Customer reports error payload snippet: `{ "error": "upstream_connect_error", "detail": "failed to connect to host (ejected)" }` They included `trace_id=7c2b4a` and `attempts=3`.
Liam (eng-sre): That looks like upstream ejection + retry exhaustion. After rollback, watch for X-Envoy-Upstream-Service-Time and `x-envoy-attempt-count` in logs. If attempts still high, we may need to temporarily increase pool size / autoscaler headroom.
Sofia (eng-platform): I've increased `min_instances` for the Dedicated pool in us-west-2 by +2 and reverted outlier thresholds. Changes deployed at 10:09 UTC.
Raj (eng-runtime): Adding a short-term mitigation: enable KV prefix caching for this customer requests to reduce load per-token on runtime. Won't help connection churn but reduces CPU pressure.
Maya (support): Passed mitigations to customer support contact. They tried again at 10:12 and saw success rate go from ~70% -> ~98%.
Nina (prod): Keep monitoring for 30m. If stable, we'll leave the pool size bumped and schedule a config review for outlier/ejection settings. Also open an RFC to document streaming client patterns + recommended keepalive headers.
Maya (support): Customer very happy with rollback and routing change. Will follow up with their logs if anything recurs. :thumbsup:
Liam (eng-sre): Followups: collect envoy admin snapshots, host ejection history, and autoscaler event timeline for postmortem. I'll start the log collection.
Sofia (eng-platform): Note for postmortem: avoid lowering minimum_hosts below 5 in multi-AZ regions for heavy streaming workloads.
Raj (eng-runtime): Add test case to stress-suite for long-lived chunked uploads + rapid concurrency to catch regressions.
infra-bot: INCIDENT-2026-0228-rlb502 created, severity=low (mitigated), owner=eng-sre"
